about: High-level design (system design) from scratch to advanced: how the web works → load balancers, caches, CDNs → databases, replication, sharding, CAP → APIs, real-time, queues, idempotency → scaling and reliability → distributed-systems fundamentals → the interview framework → classic designs (URL shortener, feed, chat, video, Uber, payments) → production (observability, deploys, security, DR) → papers, design docs and mock interviews. Many builds apply the ideas to your own Level Up app. Links checked 2026-10-12.

levels.title: How the web works
levels.goal: Know exactly what happens between a click and a response.

lessons.title: Client–server, DNS and HTTP
lessons.learn: A request goes through DNS, a TCP (and TLS) connection, an HTTP request and response. Every design sits on top of this.
lessons.build: Trace one request to your Level Up app in browser devtools: method, status, headers, timing breakdown; write it down step by step.
lessons.check: What happens, step by step, when you type a URL and press Enter?

lessons.title: TCP, TLS and HTTP/2 and 3
lessons.learn: Connections, handshakes, head-of-line blocking, and why HTTP/3 runs on QUIC.
lessons.build: Make a table comparing HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3: connections, head-of-line blocking, transport.
lessons.check: Why did HTTP/3 move to QUIC over UDP?

lessons.title: Latency numbers and back-of-the-envelope estimates
lessons.learn: Rough numbers (memory vs disk vs network, QPS, storage) let you size a system in minutes.
links: Latency numbers every programmer should know
lessons.build: Estimate storage and QPS for a 10M-user photo app (uploads per day, average size, read:write ratio) and show your maths.
lessons.check: Roughly how much slower is a disk seek than a memory read?

lessons.title: Checkpoint: draw Level Up's architecture
lessons.learn: Diagrams are how designs are communicated. The C4 model gives clear levels: context, containers, components.
lessons.build: Draw Level Up as a C4 container diagram: browser, Express API, SQL Server, PM2, Telegram, Gemini, LinkedIn, job boards.
lessons.check: Which single component failing would hurt most, and why?

levels.title: Core building blocks
levels.goal: Know the boxes every design is built from.

lessons.title: Load balancers and reverse proxies
lessons.learn: Spread traffic across servers (round robin, least connections), health checks, and layer 4 vs layer 7.
lessons.build: Run two copies of a small Node server behind nginx in Docker with round robin, kill one, and watch traffic shift.
lessons.check: Layer 4 vs layer 7 load balancing: what can each one see?

lessons.title: Caching
lessons.learn: Cache-aside, write-through, TTLs and eviction. The hard part is invalidation.
lessons.build: Add a 30-second in-memory cache to Level Up's GET /api/game (cache-aside), clear it on writes, and measure response time before and after.
lessons.check: What's the hardest part of caching, and how did you handle it?

lessons.title: CDNs and object storage
lessons.learn: Static files and media belong in object storage behind a CDN, close to users.
lessons.build: Sketch where Level Up's meal photos would live at scale: object storage, a CDN and signed URLs.
lessons.check: Why serve images from a CDN instead of your API servers?

lessons.title: API gateways and service discovery
lessons.learn: One entry point for routing, auth, rate limits and TLS in front of many services.
links: Azure Architecture Center: Gateway Routing pattern
lessons.build: List what an API gateway would handle if Level Up were split into 4 services (auth, rate limits, routing, TLS).
lessons.check: What's the risk of putting too much logic in the gateway?

levels.title: Data at scale
levels.goal: Choose the right database and scale it.

lessons.title: SQL vs NoSQL and data modelling
lessons.learn: Relational models for consistency and joins; document, key-value, wide-column and graph stores for other access patterns.
lessons.build: Model Level Up's meals in SQL and as documents; list 3 queries and which model serves each better.
lessons.check: When is a relational database the wrong choice?

lessons.title: Indexes and query performance
lessons.learn: B-tree indexes, covering indexes and execution plans: most "slow database" problems are missing or wrong indexes.
lessons.build: Find the slowest Level Up query with SQL Server's execution plan, add an index, and compare logical reads.
lessons.check: Why can an index make writes slower?

lessons.title: Replication and consistency
lessons.learn: Leader–follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication, replication lag, and consistency models.
lessons.build: Explain leader–follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication with one real database example each.
lessons.check: What is replication lag, and how can a user notice it?

lessons.title: Sharding and consistent hashing
lessons.learn: Split data across machines by key; consistent hashing keeps reshuffling small when nodes change.
lessons.build: Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes; add and remove a node and measure how many keys move.
lessons.check: Why do virtual nodes improve consistent hashing?

lessons.title: CAP, PACELC and transactions
lessons.learn: During a partition you choose consistency or availability; otherwise latency vs consistency. ACID vs BASE.
lessons.build: Classify SQL Server, Cassandra, DynamoDB and MongoDB by their CAP/PACELC choices, with a one-line reason each.
lessons.check: During a network partition, what does a CP system give up?

lessons.title: REST, gRPC and GraphQL
lessons.learn: Three API styles with different trade-offs in payload size, typing, tooling and flexibility.
lessons.build: Design the same "get today's plan" API as REST, gRPC (a .proto file) and GraphQL; compare payloads and versioning.
lessons.check: When would you choose gRPC over REST?

lessons.title: Real-time: polling, SSE and WebSockets
lessons.learn: Short polling, long polling, server-sent events and WebSockets: pick by direction and scale.
lessons.build: Push the focus-timer state from Level Up's server to the browser with Server-Sent Events instead of polling.
lessons.check: Why do WebSockets complicate load balancing?

lessons.title: Message queues and pub/sub
lessons.learn: Queues decouple producers from consumers and absorb spikes; pub/sub fans one event out to many subscribers.
lessons.build: Run Kafka or RabbitMQ in Docker; publish "meal logged" events and consume them in two services (totals, notifications).
lessons.check: Queue vs pub/sub: who receives each message?

lessons.title: Idempotency, retries and delivery guarantees
lessons.learn: Networks fail, so clients retry; idempotency keys make retries safe. At-least-once plus idempotency beats chasing exactly-once.
links: Stripe: Designing robust APIs with idempotency
AWS Builders' Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
lessons.build: Add an Idempotency-Key to one Level Up POST so a retried request never logs a meal twice, and test it.
lessons.check: Why is "exactly-once delivery" mostly a myth?

levels.title: Scalability and reliability
levels.goal: Stay fast and available under load and failure.

lessons.title: Horizontal scaling and stateless services
lessons.learn: Scale out by adding identical stateless servers; push state to databases, caches and object storage.
lessons.build: List what would stop Level Up running as 3 instances (in-process timers, local uploads, in-memory state) and how to fix each.
lessons.check: Why must web servers be stateless to scale horizontally?

lessons.title: Rate limiting and load shedding
lessons.learn: Protect services from overload: limit per client, and shed low-priority work before everything slows down.
links: Stripe: Scaling your API with rate limiters
AWS Builders' Library: Using load shedding to avoid overload
lessons.build: Add a per-minute token-bucket limit to Level Up's Gemini-backed endpoints with a friendly 429 message.
lessons.check: Where should rate limiting live: client, gateway or service?

lessons.title: Circuit breakers, timeouts and bulkheads
lessons.learn: Fail fast when a dependency is down, isolate failures, and never wait forever.
links: Azure Architecture Center: Circuit Breaker pattern
lessons.build: Wrap Level Up's Gemini client in a circuit breaker (open after 3 failures, half-open after 60 s) and log its state changes.
lessons.check: What does the half-open state protect against?

lessons.title: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
lessons.learn: Measure what users feel, set targets, and use the error budget to balance speed and stability.
links: Google SRE book: Service level objectives
lessons.build: Define 2 SLIs and SLOs for Level Up (API latency, Telegram processing delay) and compute last week's values from the logs.
lessons.check: What do you do when the error budget runs out?

levels.title: Distributed systems fundamentals
levels.goal: Understand the hard problems under every big system.

lessons.title: Time, clocks and ordering
lessons.learn: Physical clocks drift; logical clocks (Lamport, vector) order events by causality.
links: Martin Kleppmann: Distributed Systems lecture notes (Cambridge)
lessons.build: Implement Lamport clocks for 3 simulated nodes exchanging messages and print a causally ordered log.
lessons.check: Why can't you trust wall-clock timestamps to order events across machines?

lessons.title: Consensus and leader election
lessons.learn: Raft gets a cluster to agree on one log despite failures, using elections and majorities.
lessons.build: Play with the Raft visualisation, then explain leader election and log replication in 10 sentences in your notes.
lessons.check: Why does Raft need a majority (quorum)?

lessons.title: Distributed transactions: 2PC and sagas
lessons.learn: Two-phase commit blocks on failures; sagas use local transactions plus compensating actions.
lessons.build: Design a booking saga (reserve seat → charge → confirm) with a compensation for each failure point.
lessons.check: Why are sagas usually preferred over two-phase commit in microservices?

lessons.title: Outbox, CDC and event sourcing
lessons.learn: Publish events reliably with the database write; store changes as an event log when history matters.
links: Azure Architecture Center: Event Sourcing pattern
lessons.build: Add a transactional outbox table to one Level Up write, so the event is published only if the database commit succeeds.
lessons.check: What problem does the outbox pattern solve?

levels.title: The system design interview
levels.goal: Run a 45-minute design interview with a clear structure.

lessons.title: The framework
lessons.learn: Requirements (functional + non-functional) → estimates → API → data model → high-level design → deep dives → bottlenecks and trade-offs.
links: Hello Interview: System Design in a Hurry
lessons.build: Write your personal framework as a one-page template with time boxes, and use it for every practice.
lessons.check: Which non-functional requirements do you always ask about?

lessons.title: Design a URL shortener
lessons.learn: Short-code generation, storage, redirects at high read QPS, caching and analytics.
lessons.build: Design it end to end: API, base62 ID generation, database, cache, redirects at 10K QPS and analytics; draw it in Excalidraw.
lessons.check: How do you avoid two long URLs getting the same short code?

lessons.title: Design a rate limiter and a unique ID generator
lessons.learn: Distributed rate limiting with a shared store, and Snowflake-style time-ordered IDs.
links: Stripe: Scaling your API with rate limiters
lessons.build: Design a distributed rate limiter (Redis + token bucket) and a Snowflake-style ID generator, and list their failure modes.
lessons.check: What happens to Snowflake IDs if a machine's clock goes backwards?

lessons.title: Design a key-value store
lessons.learn: Partitioning, replication with N/R/W quorums, conflict handling and hinted handoff: Dynamo's ideas.
lessons.build: Design a Dynamo-style key-value store: partitioning, replication (N, R, W), conflict handling and hinted handoff.
lessons.check: With N = 3, which R and W values give strong consistency?

levels.title: Classic designs
levels.goal: Practise the systems interviewers ask most.

lessons.title: News feed
lessons.learn: Fan-out on write vs on read, the celebrity problem, ranking and caching.
lessons.build: Design a feed with fan-out on write vs read, a fix for celebrities, ranking and caching.
lessons.check: When does fan-out on write break down?

lessons.title: Chat system (WhatsApp)
lessons.learn: Persistent connections, message storage, ordering, receipts and offline sync.
links: Discord: How Discord stores trillions of messages
lessons.build: Design 1:1 and group chat: WebSocket gateways, message storage, delivered/read receipts and offline sync.
lessons.check: How do you guarantee message order within a conversation?

lessons.title: Video streaming (YouTube/Netflix)
lessons.learn: Upload, transcoding pipelines, adaptive bitrate streaming and CDNs.
lessons.build: Design upload → transcoding (queue + workers) → adaptive bitrate (HLS) → CDN, and estimate storage per hour of video.
lessons.check: Why encode each video into multiple bitrates?

lessons.title: Ride hailing and proximity (Uber)
lessons.learn: Frequent location updates, geospatial indexing and matching riders to drivers.
links: Uber: H3, a hexagonal hierarchical spatial index
lessons.build: Design driver location updates and nearby-driver search with geohash or H3 indexing, plus a matching service.
lessons.check: How do geospatial indexes make "find nearby" queries fast?

lessons.title: Typeahead and web crawler
lessons.learn: Prefix search with tries and top-K caching; a polite distributed crawler with a URL frontier.
lessons.build: Design a typeahead (trie + top-K cache), then a polite distributed crawler with a URL frontier and deduplication.
lessons.check: How does a crawler avoid hammering one website?

lessons.title: Payment system
lessons.learn: Idempotent APIs, a double-entry ledger, reconciliation, and moving money exactly once in practice.
links: AWS Builders' Library: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
Stripe: Designing robust APIs with idempotency
lessons.build: Design a payment flow with a double-entry ledger, idempotent APIs and a daily reconciliation job.
lessons.check: Why use a double-entry ledger for payments?

levels.title: Production engineering
levels.goal: Observe, deploy, secure and pay for real systems.

lessons.title: Observability: logs, metrics, traces
lessons.learn: The three signals, correlation IDs, and percentiles (p95/p99) instead of averages.
lessons.build: Add a request ID and timing to every Level Up API log line, then chart p95 latency per route for one day.
lessons.check: What can a trace show that logs can't?

lessons.title: Deployments: blue-green and canary
lessons.learn: Release safely: switch traffic between environments or roll out to a small slice first, with fast rollback.
lessons.build: Write a deploy plan for Level Up with a canary step and an automatic rollback trigger.
lessons.check: Which metric would trigger your rollback?

lessons.title: Security: authentication, authorization, secrets
lessons.learn: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, least privilege, secret storage and the OWASP Top 10.
lessons.build: Threat-model Level Up's LinkedIn OAuth and API: list 5 risks from the OWASP Top 10 with a mitigation for each.
lessons.check: What's the difference between authentication and authorization?

lessons.title: Multi-region, disaster recovery and cost
lessons.learn: RPO and RTO, backups, active-passive vs active-active, and the cost of each.
lessons.build: Define RPO and RTO for Level Up, pick a backup and disaster-recovery plan, and estimate its monthly cloud cost.
lessons.check: Active-active vs active-passive: what's the trade-off?

levels.title: Learning from real systems
levels.goal: Read how the best teams build at scale, and design like a senior engineer.

lessons.title: Read the classic papers
lessons.learn: Dynamo, Bigtable and MapReduce shaped modern databases and data processing.
lessons.build: Read the Dynamo paper and write a one-page summary: the problem, design choices, trade-offs, and what you'd change today.
lessons.check: Which Dynamo idea do modern databases still use?

lessons.title: Engineering blogs and architecture write-ups
lessons.learn: Real designs, real constraints, real trade-offs: the best way to build intuition.
lessons.build: Read 3 architecture posts from different companies; for each, note the problem, the solution and one trade-off.
lessons.check: Which pattern appeared in more than one of the posts?

lessons.title: Write a design doc
lessons.learn: Senior engineers communicate in design docs: context, goals, non-goals, design, alternatives, risks.
lessons.build: Write a design doc for one real Level Up feature (for example multi-device sync) with goals, non-goals, alternatives and risks.
lessons.check: Why do design docs list non-goals?

lessons.title: Mock interviews and portfolio
lessons.learn: Timed practice out loud is what turns knowledge into interview performance.
links: Hello Interview: System Design in a Hurry
lessons.build: Do 3 timed mock designs (record yourself), publish the diagrams and notes in a system-design repo, and write a LinkedIn post about one.
lessons.check: Which part of the interview do you rush, and how will you fix it?
